actual_item.title: The Hecke Jucys-Murphy action is dominance triangular
actual_item.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, and let $L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements ([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$, every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist $a_v\in R$ with $$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$ where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard $\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]], [[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values. Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in $L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.
actual_item.strategy: Induct on $n$ and then on $k$ exactly as in the source. If $k$ lies in a non-last row of $t$, delete the last row and apply the induction hypothesis to the smaller partition; if $k$ is not in the first column, use $m_tL_k=m_t(1+L_{k-1}T_{k-1})$ together with the induction on $k$ and the quadratic relation; the remaining case (last row and first column) is handled by writing $m_t=hm_{\mu'}$ with $\mu'=(\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_r,1)$ and applying the Garnir relation Lemma 3.31 plus the induction hypothesis. The statement is for the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]), whose basis is $m_t=m_{t^\lambda t}$, so that the correction terms $m_{v^\lambda v}$ of the source's printed identity $m_{st}L_k=[\operatorname{res}_t(k)]_qm_{st}+\sum_{v\rhd t}r_vm_{sv}$ are the module basis vectors; the same triangularity in the Murphy-basis normalisation is [[Hu-Mathas]] Lemma 3.12 with (3.8). This is Mathas, Theorem 3.30 (Dipper-James) with Proposition 3.24 and Corollary 3.25. No choice is used.

actual_item.title: Separated Hecke residues give seminormal idempotents and bases
actual_item.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, let $e=e(F,q)$ and assume $e>n$ (with $e=\infty$ allowed); let $\lambda\vdash n$, $H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$, and let $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ be the Murphy cell module with Murphy basis $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]).
1. (**Separation**) If $s,t$ are standard $\lambda$-tableaux with $[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q$ for all $1\le k\le n$ then $s=t$. More precisely, if the q-content values agree for all $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$ for some $i$, then $s=t$ or $t=s(i\ i+1)$.
2. (**Idempotents**) For a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ define, inside the commutative algebra $F[L_1,\dots,L_n]$, $$F_t:=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\ \prod_{\substack{s\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\\[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q\ne[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q}}\frac{L_k-[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q}{[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q-[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q}$$ and put $f_t:=m_tF_t\in S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$. All denominators are nonzero by (1) and the $f_t$ are well-defined spectral projectors: $f_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,f_t$, and $f_t=m_t+\sum_{s\rhd t}a_sm_s$ for suitable $a_s\in F$.
3. (**Orthogonal seminormal basis**) $\{f_t:t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is a basis of $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ satisfying $f_tF_s=\delta_{ts}f_t$ and $\langle f_s,f_t\rangle_\lambda=\delta_{st}\langle f_t,f_t\rangle_\lambda$; it is the **seminormal basis** of the Murphy cell module.
4. (**Generator action**) Let $s$ be a standard $\lambda$-tableau, $1\le i<n$ and $t:=s(i\ i+1)$, and put $\rho:=\operatorname{content}_s(i)-\operatorname{content}_s(i+1)\in\mathbb Z$ (an integer; it equals $\operatorname{res}_s(i)-\operatorname{res}_t(i)$ in the source's notation). If $i$ and $i+1$ lie in the same row of $s$ then $f_sT_i=q\,f_s$; if they lie in the same column then $f_sT_i=-f_s$; otherwise $t$ is standard and $$f_sT_i=\alpha_i(s)\,f_t-\frac{1}{[\rho]_q}f_s,\qquad \alpha_i(s):=\begin{cases}1,&s\rhd t,\\[1mm]\dfrac{[1+\rho]_q[1-\rho]_q}{[\rho]_q[-\rho]_q},&t\rhd s,\end{cases}$$ where $[-\rho]_q$ is the extended quantum integer of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]] and for the swapped tableau $\operatorname{content}_t(i)-\operatorname{content}_t(i+1)=-\rho$. No semisimplicity of $H$ is assumed and no choice principle is used.
actual_item.strategy: (1) is Lemma 3.32: when $e>n$ the nodes of equal $e$-residue lie on diagonal lines, so distinct removable nodes have distinct residues, and peeling off $n,n-1,\dots,1$ determines $t$ from its q-content sequence. (2),(3) are Proposition 3.33 and Theorem 3.34: the triangularity of [[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] makes $F_t$ a projector annihilating strictly dominating tableaux; comparing $f_sL_k$ directly and using the associativity of the cellular form ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) gives $f_sF_t=\delta_{st}f_t$ and orthogonality. (4) is the coefficient computation of Theorem 3.34(ii): $f_sT_i$ is an eigenvector of every $L_k$ with $k\ne i,i+1$, so by (1) it lies in $\mathrm{span}(f_s,f_t)$; writing $f_sT_i=\alpha_i(s)f_t+c_sf_s$ and multiplying on the right by $L_i$ recovers $c_s=-1/[\rho]_q$ from the relation $T_iL_i=T_iL_{i+1}-1-(q-1)L_{i+1}$ of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]], and the quadratic relation $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$ gives the product $\alpha_i(s)\alpha_i(t)=[1+\rho]_q[1-\rho]_q/([\rho]_q[-\rho]_q)$ for the swapped tableau $t$; since $\operatorname{content}_t(i)-\operatorname{content}_t(i+1)=-\rho$, the two standard cases have $\rho>0$ with $s\rhd t$ (branch $1$) and $\rho<0$ with $t\rhd s$ (branch $[1+\rho][1-\rho]/([\rho][-\rho])$). The stated branch assignment is the Mathas-Murphy seminormal coefficient system of Hu-Mathas (Example 3.11 with the axial distance (3.8), Lemma 3.12 and Proposition 3.17), which we verified directly in $H(S_3)$ ($\rho=2$, $q=3,5,7$) and $H(S_4)$ ($\rho=3$, $q=2$); the display of Theorem 3.34(ii) in the 1998 prepublication manuscript is inconsistent with the Hecke relations in the $t\rhd s$ case (exact computation in the batch notes), so the item uses the corrected form. The abstract cellular-algebra form of the same spectral construction is checked independently in Mathas-Soriano (separation condition, Proposition 4.13 and the appendix). No choice is used.

actual_item.title: Hecke Specht theory specialises to group Specht theory at q = 1
actual_item.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q=1\in F$, and let $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ be the specialization of the generic type-A Hecke algebra at $v\mapsto1$, so that $H_{F,1}(S_n)\cong F[S_n]$ with $T_w\mapsto w$ ([[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]). Then the Hecke theory of this page specializes as follows.
1. The Murphy elements $m_\mu=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w$ specialize to the row symmetrizers $\sum_{w\in S_\mu}w$, and the Murphy basis $\{m_{st}\}$ of $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ specializes to the Murphy basis of the group algebra $F[S_n]$ (the base change $\mathbb Z[S_n]\to F[S_n]$ of the integral Murphy basis).
2. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ the specialization of the page's Hecke Specht module $S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) is the ordinary Specht module in the Dipper-James convention: $S^{\lambda}_{q=1}\cong S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ as $F[S_n]$-modules, with the standard polytabloid basis ([[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]); the specialized cell form is the standard bilinear form on $S^{\lambda}_k$ whose radical defines the James quotient $D^{\lambda}$ ([[def-modular-specht-form-and-radical-quotient]]).
3. The quantum characteristic of $q=1$ is $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)>0$, and $e=\infty$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)=0$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); in characteristic $p>0$ a partition is $e$-regular exactly when it is $p$-regular. Hence $D^{\lambda}_{q=1}\ne0$ exactly for $p$-regular $\lambda$ ([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]), and for non-$p$-regular $\lambda$ one has $\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}=S^{\lambda}$, so not every Specht module remains simple in characteristic $p$. This matches the group-side classification [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]] and the conjugate-sign dictionary [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]. In characteristic $0$ the specialization is split semisimple and all Specht modules are irreducible.
actual_item.strategy: Base-change the Murphy cellular basis along $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to F$, $v\mapsto1$: the structure constants are polynomials in $q$, so specialization gives a cellular basis of $F[S_n]$, and the cell modules specialize to the modules with the specialized triangular multiplication. The identification with the Dipper-James Specht module uses the printed p. 25 convention warning of the source together with the conjugate-sign duality of [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]; the polytabloid/Murphy basis comparison is [[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]. The simple-label statement is the specialization of [[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]] at $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$, compared with [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]. The direction of information is one-way (this item imports the group classification and no group-side item depends on the Hecke theory). No choice is used.

actual_item.title: The q-Schur Weyl weight-space Gram determinant is a hook product
actual_item.statement: Let $R$ be an integral domain, $q\in R^{\times}$, $d,n\ge1$, and let $S(d,n)$ be the q-Schur algebra with Weyl modules $W^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). For a partition $\lambda$ of $n$ with at most $d$ parts and a weight (composition of $n$ with at most $d$ parts) $\mu$, let $G^{\lambda}_{\mu}\in R$ be the determinant of the Gram matrix of the cell form of $W^{\lambda}$ restricted to its $\mu$-weight space, computed with respect to the semistandard basis. Let $\beta=\beta(\lambda)=(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)$ be the beta sequence $\beta_i=\lambda'_i+n-i$ of $\lambda$ ([[def-alternating-weyl-and-specht-symbols-from-beta-sequences]], [[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]) and let $h^{\lambda}_{ab}=\lambda_a-b+\lambda'_b-a+1$ be the hook length of the node $(a,b)\in[\lambda]$, with leg length $l^\lambda_{ab}$ ([[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]]). Then $$G^{\lambda}_{\mu}=q^{N}\prod_{\substack{(a,b),(a,c)\in[\lambda]\\ b<c}}\left(\frac{[h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_q}{[h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_q}\right)^{d_{\mu}(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_b+h^{\lambda}_{ab},\dots,\beta_c-h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots,\beta_n)},$$ where $N=N(\lambda,\mu)$ is the explicit integer $\sum_T\ell(d(\mathrm{last}(T)))$ summed over the semistandard $\lambda$-tableaux $T$ of type $\mu$ (the degree of the corresponding semistandard basis vector), $d_{\mu}$ is the signed semistandard multiplicity of [[def-alternating-weyl-and-specht-symbols-from-beta-sequences]] and $[\ \ ]_q$ are the quantum integers ([[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]). The exponent has the exact combinatorial interpretation of Lemma 5.26: $$d_{\mu}(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_b+h^{\lambda}_{ab},\dots,\beta_c-h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots,\beta_n)=(-1)^{l^{\lambda}_{ab}+l^{\lambda}_{ac}}\,|T_0(\eta,\mu)|$$ whenever $\eta$ is obtained from $\lambda$ by unwrapping the removable border strip $R^{\lambda}_{ac}$ (the hook of $(a,c)$, of size $h^{\lambda}_{ac}$) and re-wrapping it with its lowest node in column $b$, and it is zero otherwise ([[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]], [[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]). The product is interpreted in $R$ after pairing all numerator and denominator factors, so the displayed formula represents an element of $R$ even though individual factors need not be units, and the theorem is stated over an integral domain, not only over a field.
actual_item.strategy: Follow the source's Theorem 5.27 with Proposition 5.24. First orthogonalise the semistandard basis to compute the norms $\langle\varphi_T,\varphi_T\rangle=q^{\ell(d(\mathrm{last}(T)))}$ (Theorem 5.18), so that the determinant is $q^Ng^{\lambda}_{\mu}$ with $g^{\lambda}_\mu$ the product over the semistandard $\lambda$-tableaux of type $\mu$ (Corollary 5.19). Then use Lemmas 5.22-5.26 to regroup the product: an exchange of two adjacent beta numbers changes the determinant by $(-1)$, repeated beta entries annihilate the alternant, and the only nonzero beta displacements $b\mapsto b-h$ are those by hook lengths; Lemma 5.26 identifies subtracting $h$ at position $b$ with unwrapping the rim hook $R^{\lambda}_{ab}$. Collecting the signed semistandard multiplicities gives exactly the displayed hook ratio with exponent $d_\mu(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_b+h^{\lambda}_{ab},\dots,\beta_c-h^{\lambda}_{ac},\dots,\beta_n)$; the hook-to-border-strip identification is [[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]. No choice is used.

actual_item.title: The Jantzen filtration of a lifted cell module
actual_item.statement: Let $R$ be a principal ideal domain ([[def-principal-ideal-domain]]) with a chosen prime element $\pi$, let $F:=R/\pi R$ be the residue field, and let $M$ be a free $R$-module of finite rank ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]) equipped with a symmetric $R$-bilinear form $\langle\ ,\ \rangle:M\times M\to R$ whose extension to the fraction field $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is non-degenerate (equivalently $\det G\ne0$ for a Gram matrix $G$ of the form). For $i\ge1$ put $$M(i):=\{x\in M:\langle x,y\rangle\in\pi^iR\ \text{for all }y\in M\},\qquad M_F(i):=(M(i)+\pi M)/\pi M\subseteq M_F:=M\otimes_RF.$$ Then $M(0)=M$, the $M(i)$ are $R$-submodules with $M(i+1)\subseteq M(i)$, the descending chain $$M_F=M_F(0)\supseteq M_F(1)\supseteq M_F(2)\supseteq\cdots$$ stabilises at $0$ (that is, $M_F(z)=0$ for all sufficiently large $z$, because $\det G\ne0$), and $M_F(1)=\mathrm{rad}\,M_F$, the radical of the reduced form. This finite descending filtration is the **Jantzen filtration** of $M$ with respect to $(R,\pi,\langle\ ,\ \rangle)$. The hypotheses are exactly: $R$ a PID, $\pi$ a prime element, the form non-degenerate over $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$; no valuation-ring or DVR hypothesis is substituted, and the prime element $\pi$, its ideal $\pi R$ and the fraction field $K$ are kept distinct.
actual_item.strategy: A definition item. Each $M(i)$ is a submodule: for the cell forms on this page the associativity identity $\langle xa,y\rangle=\langle x,ya^*\rangle$ shows closedness under the action. Reduction gives a descending chain of finite-dimensional $F$-spaces, so it stabilises; $\det G\ne0$ makes the stable value $0$ because a vector whose pairing with every basis vector lies in all $\pi^iR$ is zero over $K$. Finally $x\in M(1)$ reduces into the radical of the reduced form by definition. This is Mathas, Chapter 5 section 2 (setup preceding Lemma 5.29), printed pp. 54-55; no choice is used.

references.title: Mathas, Iwahori-Hecke Algebras and Schur Algebras of the Symmetric Group, Chapter 5 section 2: the Jantzen filtration over a PID, printed pp. 54-55

direct_affected_consumers.assessment: Only associativity, Gram form and divisibility. NEW50 exact unit preserves the filtration.

actual_item.title: General type-A decomposition numbers remain unsolved
actual_item.statement:
The two preceding constraints on the decomposition matrix of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ are real but limited, and neither solves the general problem. (i) Dominance unitriangularity ([[cor-type-a-hecke-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular]]) determines only the diagonal entries $d_{\mu\mu}=1$ and the vanishing region $d_{\lambda\mu}
e0\Rightarrow\mu\unrhd\lambda$; it gives no value for an off-diagonal entry. (ii) The q-Schaper/Jantzen sum formula ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]]) is a virtual radical-layer identity whose coefficients $
u_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_{\hat q})-
u_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_{\hat q})$ bound the corresponding composition multiplicities from above; it neither determines a general multiplicity nor produces a positive combinatorial rule. Special coefficient regimes and low-rank calculations determine additional entries (canonically based, weight-one, and small-$n$ cases), but the classification of irreducible Specht modules in arbitrary positive characteristic is a known open problem, and no general closed formula for the decomposition numbers of $S_n$ in a fixed positive characteristic is claimed anywhere on this page. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.
actual_item.strategy: Compare exactly what the two cited results determine, and record the boundary without asserting any unproved classification. Provenance: statement literature-derived, proof not-applicable; the remark is not consumed to prove any replacement.

actual_item.title: q-Schur Weyl modules are in the same block iff their labels have the same e-core
actual_item.statement: Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]], [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]), let $d\ge n$, and let $W^{\lambda}_F$ be the Weyl modules of $S_F(d,n)$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Then for partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ with at most $d$ parts, $W^{\lambda}_F$ and $W^{\mu}_F$ lie in the same block of $S_F(d,n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Consequently the blocks of $S_F(d,n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|\le n$ and $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $W^{\lambda}_F$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. (For $e=\infty$ every partition is its own core and every Weyl module is its own block, the algebra being semisimple.)
actual_item.strategy:
Work with a principal ideal domain $R$, a prime $\pi\in R$ and a lift $\hat q\in R^{	imes}$ of $q$ with $[n]!_{\hat q}
e0$; such a lift always exists (for instance $R=F[X]$ localised at the prime ideal $(X-q)$, $\pi=X-q$, $\hat q=X$), and then $
u_\pi([h]_{\hat q})
e0$ exactly when $[h]_q=0$ in $F$, i.e. when $e\mid h$. Use the Jantzen sum formula in the exact form of [[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]], $\sum_{i>0}[W^{\lambda}_F(i)]=\sum_{(a,b),(a,c)} igl(
u_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_{\hat q})-
u_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_{\hat q}) igr)[W^{ eta(\lambda)+h^{\lambda}_{ab}e_b-h^{\lambda}_{ac}e_c}_F]$, and the block-separation lemma [[lem-virtual-weyl-combinations-detect-q-schur-block-separation]]. (1) Necessity: the layers $W^{\lambda}_F(i)$ are submodules of $W^{\lambda}_F$, so all their composition factors lie in the block of $W^{\lambda}_F$; if $W^{\mu}_F$ occurs with nonzero coefficient in the sum formula then $
u_\pi([h]_{\hat q})
e0$ for at least one of $h=h^{\lambda}_{ab},h^{\lambda}_{ac}$, hence $e$ divides at least one of these hook lengths. The index $\mu$ is obtained from $\lambda$ by unwrapping the rim hook $R^{\lambda}_{ac}$ and wrapping it back lower at column $b$ (the source's Lemma 5.26), so when $e\mid h^{\lambda}_{ac}$ or $e\mid h^{\lambda}_{ab}$ the move proceeds along $e$-hooks and $C_e(\mu)=C_e(\lambda)$ by the core theorem. The Jantzen sum formula and linear independence of Weyl classes show that the block of $W^{\lambda}_F$ is generated by these Jantzen links (the source's Proposition 2.9 in Lyle-Mathas), so transitivity gives the only-if direction. (2) Sufficiency: fix $\gamma$ and let $\lambda$ be the partition with core $\gamma$ obtained from $\gamma$ by adjoining all $we$ boxes to the first row, where $w=w_e(\lambda)$. For any other $\mu$ with core $\gamma$, some rim hook $R^{\mu}_{ab}$ of length $e$ has its lowest node below the first row; removing it and re-adding it at the end of the first row produces a partition $\mu'$ that appears with nonzero multiplicity in the Jantzen sum for $W^{\mu}_F$, so the block lemma links $W^{\mu}_F$ and $W^{\mu'}_F$; induction on the dominance distance to $\lambda$ gives that all Weyl modules of the core class lie in one block. This is Mathas, Theorem 5.36 with its printed proof (printed pp. 60-62), independently organised by Lyle-Mathas, Propositions 2.3 and 2.9. No choice principle is used.

actual_item.title: Nakayama block classification for symmetric groups
actual_item.statement: Let $k$ be a splitting field of characteristic $p>0$ (equivalently the residue field of the fixed splitting $p$-modular system, [[def-splitting-p-modular-system-for-a-finite-group]], [[def-p-blocks-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]) and let $n\ge0$. Two Specht modules $S^{\lambda}_k,S^{\mu}_k$ of $k[S_n]$ lie in the same block of $k[S_n]$ if and only if $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ have the same $p$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Consequently the blocks of $k[S_n]$ are indexed by the pairs $(\gamma,w)$ with $\gamma$ a $p$-core, $w\in\mathbb N_0$ and $n=|\gamma|+pw$, and the block of $S^{\lambda}_k$ is $(c_p(\lambda),w_p(\lambda))$ with $w_p(\lambda)=(n-|c_p(\lambda)|)/p$ ([[prop-core-quotient-size-and-weight-formula]]).
actual_item.strategy: Specialise the Hecke block theorem at $q=1$. By [[prop-hecke-specht-theory-specializes-to-group-specht-theory-at-q-one]] the specialisation $H_{k,1}(S_n)\cong k[S_n]$ carries the Hecke Specht modules of this page to the group Specht modules of $k[S_n]$ in the Dipper-James convention and has quantum characteristic $e=\operatorname{char}(k)=p$, so [[cor-type-a-hecke-specht-modules-are-in-the-same-block-iff-their-labels-have-the-same-e-core]] gives: $S^{\lambda}_k$ and $S^{\mu}_k$ lie in the same block of $k[S_n]$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $p$-core. The parametrisation by pairs $(\gamma,w)$ is then the size formula of [[prop-core-quotient-size-and-weight-formula]] at $e=p$ together with the block decomposition by primitive central idempotents in [[def-p-blocks-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]. This is Mathas, Corollary 5.37 specialised at $q=1$ (printed pp. 61-63 with Chapters 1 and 3-5); O'Donovan, Theorem 1 (arXiv:1708.04365, p. 1) states the same classification by the independent Young-module and Brauer-quotient route and is recorded here as an independent confirmation of the statement, not as the proof route of this page. No choice principle is used.

actual_item.title: The complete weight-one decomposition matrix for S3 at p=3
actual_item.statement: Take $e=p=3$ and the weight-one configuration $n=3$, $\gamma=\varnothing$ of [[thm-weight-one-block-decomposition-pattern]]; the three partitions of $3$ with $3$-core $\varnothing$ are $\lambda_1=(3)\rhd\lambda_2=(2,1)\rhd\lambda_3=(1,1,1)$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). The block of $S_3$ at $p=3$ therefore has the complete decomposition matrix, in the source's Weyl/simple normalisation and with rows and columns in the order $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$, equal to $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$; applying the Schur functor and the conjugation/duality dictionary gives the Murphy Specht rows $[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]$, which in the page's $3$-regular labels $(3),(2,1)$ is the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ with rows $(3),(2,1),(1,1,1)$ ([[thm-nakayama-block-classification-for-symmetric-groups]], [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]); the group-side entries are verified directly from the two-dimensional model $S^{(2,1)}$ of characteristic $3$, whose all-ones vector spans a trivial submodule with sign quotient, together with $S^{(3)}=\operatorname{triv}$ and $S^{(1,1,1)}=\operatorname{sgn}$.
actual_item.strategy: List the partitions of $3$ with $3$-core $\varnothing$: $(3)$ and $(1,1,1)$ remove their unique $3$-hook and $(2,1)$ has no $3$-hook, giving exactly the three labels in the stated dominance order. Apply the weight-one theorem to obtain the bidiagonal Weyl matrix, then the Schur functor and the conjugation/duality dictionary $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=(S^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^{*}$, $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^{*}$ to pass from the Murphy rows to the group-side matrix with rows and columns in the $p$-regular labels $(3),(2,1)$, and finally compare with the direct computation from the standard module: in characteristic $3$ the all-ones vector of $S^{(2,1)}$ spans a trivial submodule with sign quotient, so the rows of $S^{(3)},S^{(2,1)},S^{(1,1,1)}$ are $(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)$ in the labels $(3),(2,1)$, and the simple labels are those of [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]. The two computations agree entry by entry, which is the verification of the example. No choice principle is used. Sources: Mathas, Proposition 5.38 and the accompanying discussion of $q=1$ (printed pp. 61-63); the published $S_3$ matrix.

actual_item.title: The Schur functor compares first-level branching with Hecke restriction
actual_item.statement: Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^\times$, $\ell$ the quantum characteristic of $q$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) and $n\ge r$ as in the source. Let $S(n,r)$ be the type-A q-Schur algebra with the idempotent $e$ of the weight $(1^r)$, so that $eS(n,r)e\cong H(r)$, and let $f_{n,r}:S(n,r)\text{-mod}\to H(r)\text{-mod}$, $V\mapsto eV$, be the exact Schur functor with left adjoint $h_{n,r}$ ([[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]]). Let $L_n(\lambda)$ be the irreducible $S(n,r)$-module for an $\ell$-restricted $\lambda\vdash r$, and $L_n(\lambda)^1$ its first level. Then (i) $f_{n-1,r-1}\bigl(L_n(\lambda)^1\bigr)=f_{n,r}\bigl(L_n(\lambda)\bigr)\bigl\downarrow_{H(r-1)}$ as $H(r-1)$-modules, naturally; (ii) for $S(n,r)$-modules $W,V$ with $W^{(e)}=W$ and $V_{(e)}=0$ one has $\operatorname{Hom}_{S(n,r)}(W,V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{H(r)}(fW,fV)$, so the functor detects and preserves the relevant Hom spaces and (being exact) transfers composition multiplicities of first-level modules; (iii) if $\lambda$ is $\ell$-restricted then the socle of $L_n(\lambda)^1$ restricted to the Levi subalgebra $U(n-1)$ consists of $\ell$-restricted labels; at $q=1$ (so $\ell=p$ in characteristic $p$; characteristic zero gives $\ell=\infty$) the specialization $H(r)\to kS_r$ of ([[prop-hecke-specht-theory-specializes-to-group-specht-theory-at-q-one]]) makes (i)-(iii) statements about $kS_r$-modules and the simple $kS_{r-1}$-modules of ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]).
actual_item.strategy: Complete argument, Brundan 1998 §5.5-5.7 (complete 34-page author manuscript, pp. 30-32) and Kleshchev I §2.12(v), whose citation is replaced by this proof-bearing comparison. (i) Take the permitted stable rank $n=r$ and write the $(1^r)$-weight idempotent of $S(n,r)$; by §3.22 of the source the weight belongs to the level-1 summand, and deleting the last (level) coordinate of the weight identifies it with the $(1^{r-1})$-weight of $S(n-1,r-1)$, while the generators $T_1,\dots,T_{r-2}$ act identically before and after the deletion. Hence both sides are equal as explicit simultaneous weight spaces, naturally in $V$; this uses neither semisimplicity nor an identification of cellular and crystal labels. (ii) Is Brundan's Lemma 5.6(i)-(ii), proved by the adjunction $h\dashv f$ and the submodule $V_{(e)}$; (iii) is Lemma 5.7, whose proof uses the good-node description of the socle and shows that $i\in R^{good}(\lambda)$ implies $\lambda(i)$ is $\ell$-restricted. Composition multiplicities: apply the exact functor $f$ to a composition series of the first-level module; a surviving restricted simple maps to a Hecke simple, a killed simple contributes nothing, and by (ii) the multiplicity of a selected surviving simple is preserved. The $q=1$ specialization is the Hecke/group identification of the batch-20 item. This is the exact replacement for Kleshchev I §2.12(v) as recorded by the SYMR-9 evidence report; Step 3 must keep the weight-idempotent computation explicit.

actual_item.title: Multipartitions with fixed component cores are cyclotomic Jantzen-connected
actual_item.statement: Under the arbitrary-field finite-e nondegenerate cyclotomic hypotheses of [[lem-cyclotomic-jantzen-equivalence-is-schur-and-hecke-block-linkage]], any two $\ell$-multipartitions of a common rank $n$ with equal componentwise $e$-cores are $J$-equivalent, even if their component sizes differ. At fixed component sizes, the full-level coefficient for a change in a single component equals its level-one coefficient. The proof consumes the actual native21 same-e-core Hecke Specht-block theorem for all ranks, not its readiness receipt, and imports no Carter-partition classification.
actual_item.strategy:
Fix the rank n and charges in the Statement. First suppose the component sizes agree. For a single component a of rank m, the actual level-one Hecke algebra is the finite Hecke algebra by [[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]. Its same-core Specht-block clause [[cor-type-a-hecke-specht-modules-are-in-the-same-block-iff-their-labels-have-the-same-e-core]], together with [[lem-cyclotomic-jantzen-equivalence-is-schur-and-hecke-block-linkage]] at level one, connects any two rank-m partitions with equal core by level-one Jantzen edges. The Dipper–James to Murphy convention change is conjugate-dual; core equality is preserved because core(transpose λ)=transpose(core λ). Thus the exact existing clause applies over the original F without an algebraic-closure hypothesis. Rank m=0 has a single empty partition and needs no block theorem.

For two full multipartitions that differ only in component a, every contributing equal-remainder hook pair in J lies in a. The common residue factor Q_a t^(na) is a unit of O. Replacing it by the level-one factor Q_a t^m also multiplies each foot difference by a Laurent unit. Hence its valuation is unchanged, and the full-level J coefficient is exactly the level-one coefficient. Insert the level-one paths in a and leave the other components fixed. Changing the components one at a time connects all equal-size-component multipartitions with the same component cores.

If component weights differ, choose a component whose weight exceeds its target and one whose weight is deficient. A positive-weight component has a removable e-hook, by its core construction. Wrap an e-hook in the deficient component with the same foot residue: for any prescribed foot residue f, moving the lowest bead on runner f−1 down by e creates such a hook, since its foot residue is the starting beta position plus1. The changed components determine the removed/added hook pair uniquely. In the appropriate dominance orientation their J contribution is one signed valuation, with no cancellation. Equal foot residue means its nonzero generic difference is divisible by t−1, so the valuation is a positive integer. Nonzero generic foot differences are part of the exact J formula supplier [[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]]; no unit-difference or characteristic-zero restriction is inserted. Thus the transfer is a Jantzen edge. It lowers the sum of squares of discrepancies of component hook weights by at least2. Finitely many such transfers equalize component weights. The preceding fixed-size argument then completes the connection. Every moved e-hook preserves the component core, and all steps preserve total rank.

actual_item.title: A graded algebra isomorphism transports the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups and its dualities
actual_item.statement:
Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift $M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. It therefore induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and $G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed anti-automorphisms $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$ (i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective Hom-dualities $\#$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives.

**Application.** For each nonzero content sector choose the actual graded block isomorphism rho_alpha. DEFINE the Hecke duality by star_H=rho_alpha star_R rho_alpha^{-1}. This is a grading-preserving anti-involution, fixing the NAMED images of e(i),y_r,psi_r, and rho_alpha intertwines it by definition. Thus the preceding duality conclusion applies blockwise. This does not identify star_H with the raw cellular anti-involution that fixes affine Hecke generators, and does not infer that a product is fixed merely because its factors are fixed.
actual_item.strategy: An algebra isomorphism gives inverse exact restriction-of-scalars functors, identity on the underlying graded vector spaces. It preserves shifts, finite dimension and finite free modules; retracts of finite free modules remain projective. Graded Hom spaces agree by the identity on maps, hence composition multiplicities, K0/G0, Cartan and forgetful maps agree. For finite duals, (a f)(m)=f(star_R(a)m) matches the transported formula because rho star_R=star_H rho; the identical substitution in Hom_R(P,R) identifies projective Hom duals. In the application define star_H by conjugation, which proves anti-multiplicativity and involutivity immediately; generator fixation is fixation of the rho-images. Products are reversed by star_H, so no claim about the raw affine-Hecke cellular star is used. This exact computation proves the transported self-dual and degree-zero head normalization clauses. No choice.

actual_item.title: The graded adjustment polynomials in positive characteristic
actual_item.statement:
In branch (CP) of the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the reduced modules $J(
u)$ of [[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]] and the normalized simples $D(\lambda)$ with crystal label $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ of the general-field normalization/crystal clauses of [[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] and [[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]] (in branch (C0) these are the heads of the graded Specht modules by [[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]] (3)), define the **graded adjustment polynomials** $a_{\lambda,
u}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ for $\lambda,
u\in RP_\alpha$ by $$[J(
u)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,
u}(q)[D(\lambda)]\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad a_{\lambda,
u}(q)=[J(
u):D(\lambda)]_q .$$ Then the matrix $(a_{\lambda,
u})$ is the graded adjustment matrix; its entries are bar-invariant, have nonnegative integer coefficients, satisfy $a_{
u,
u}(q)=1$ and vanish unless $\lambda\unlhd
u$ (dominance); equivalently $a_{\lambda,
u}$ is the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in $(\Psi_{m can}^{m Hecke})^{-1}(D_
u)$.

**Source comparison (recorded, not used).** For level one and $\xi=1$ the source states that this adjustment matrix specializes at $q=1$ to the adjustment matrix of James; that degenerate comparison lies outside the nondegenerate branch of this page and is deferred (see the batch coverage record). No choice is used in the definition.
actual_item.strategy: Expand the actual finite-dimensional J(nu) in the shift-orbit basis of normalized positive-characteristic simples; this uniquely defines the Laurent coefficients and makes their coefficients nonnegative integers. The general-field cover/duality/crystal suppliers normalize these simples; the local CP head/crystal lemma identifies their labels with the cellular-head labels, without using the characteristic-zero-only global theorem in CP. The local CP comparison proves J(nu)=D(nu)+terms with smaller labels, giving diagonal1 and dominance support. Bar invariance follows from WORD CHARACTERS: the characteristic-zero normalized simple is finite-dual self-dual, so each word graded dimension is symmetric in q. J(nu) has this same character, and D_psi J(nu) has the inverted character, hence the same one. The actual extremal-word character detection implies equality of their G0 classes. Applying duality to the expansion fixes every normalized simple and inverts q, so uniqueness gives a(q)=a(q^-1). No self-dual stable integral lattice, field-bar compatibility of an unspecified form, or positive-characteristic global-basis theorem is assumed. The source's degenerate comparison remains recorded outside this page's parameter branch. No new choice.
